newsitem.title: GERMANY: German banks see calm prices in 97, no rate rise.
newsitem.headline: German banks see calm prices in 97, no rate rise.

text.p: Germany's top banking federation on Tuesday said inflation was likely to remain modest throughout 1997 and there was minimal risk that the Bundesbank would tighten its monetary policy.
In a monthly report, the BdB group, which represents Germany's biggest commercial banks, predicted that German inflation would remain below two percent this year, making a rate hike unnecessary.
"The relaxed inflation climate, especially the outlook for continued moderate inflation development, have created an ideal environment for low capital market rates," the BdB said.

The only potential risk threat for price stability would arise from further gains in the dollar against the mark, the BdB warned. Should the dollar rise above the 1.80 mark-level, some risk might arise.
Turning to the U.S., the BdB said a rate hike there would not necessarily hammer prices on the U.S. bond market, especially if a hike were interpreted as a means of controlling inflation risks.
